title: Selling Your Business? Don’t Let Diligence Exhaust You

 Selling Your Business? Keep Diligence From Killing Your Deal
Hi Sara,
Thinking about selling your business? Buckle up – because the diligence process is where deals are made…or broken.
But don’t worry, I’m here to break it down into real talk – no corporate jargon, no stress headaches (well, fewer of those, anyway).
Step1: Sign That NDA – Seriously
Before you share anything, get an NDA in place. That client list you built with sweat and caffeine? You don’t want it floating around. Protect it.
Step 2: The Buyer’s Checklist – AKA, Your New Homework
Once you find a buyer, they’ll hand you a checklist that looks like it was written by someone with a PhD in Overwhelming You. Don’t freak out. It’s a catch-all list. Some stuff won’t apply to you. Drop “n/a” on the things that don’t apply like environmental concerns and tackle the rest. Completing the checklist should be a collaborative process, so delegate everything to the Buyer where you can. Weekly calls can help keep momentum.
Step 3: The Virtual Data Room – Less of a Vault, More of a Beat Up Filing Cabinet
Upload your docs to a Virtual Data Room (VDR). Think of it as a digital safe deposit box for your business secrets. This is what the buyer will comb through to build the purchase agreement later.
Step 4: The Purchase Agreement – Your Business, in Legalese
Everything you upload becomes part of this holy grail document – complete with “schedules” (fancy term for all the details). This is what locks in the deal. The Schedules are very protective for you, you want to add as much detail as you can to them. This is the one easy thing too many sellers leave on the table.
Pro Tip: Keep Your Golden Goose Safe
Your client list? That’s your crown jewel. Don’t hand it over until the deal is signed, sealed, and delivered. No early peeks.
Deals Fall Through – Stay Ready
Not every deal closes. Keep your data room organized and maintain a good copy so you’re prepped for the next buyer if needed. I promise the second round is easier!
Call in the Pros (That’s What We’re Here For)
Lean on your lawyer and other experts to avoid expensive mistakes. You don’t want to be the person who sells their business only to get sued when you were supposed to be sailing off into the sunset.
Selling your business is a long elaborate process. It’s part paperwork, part poker face, and a lot of “Why is this checklist so long?” But with the right team and the right prep, you’ll get to that smooth transition – and maybe even a celebratory drink after.
Got questions? Thinking about selling? Check out our courses here on Deal Academy to help you get started. 
To smarter deals,
Sara Sharp
Partner, SK&S Law Group
Business Consultant and Founder of Deal Academy
